publication.title: Multi-source thermal and performance data for thermal fault diagnosis in marine diesel engines
publication.data_access_status: No direct dataset repository or archive download was identified in the accessible public metadata. Request the data package and its license/manifest from the authors before attempting a score reproduction.

reported_dataset.signal_representation: 24-dimensional high-frequency transient gas-path parameters plus in-cylinder steady-state performance indicators

source_domains.role: engine test-bench measurements including industrial background noise
real-vessel telemetry with wave-induced load fluctuations and engine-room interference
superimposed fault data produced through virtual-real fusion to represent severe sea-state effects
source_domains.physical_status: synthetic/virtual-real composite, not an observed shipboard fault event

published_transfer_result.protocol_detail_status: full split, class counts, per-domain membership and uncertainty have not yet been independently audited

benchmark_tracks.primary_question: How much transfer degrades when calibrated simulation meets industrial measurement noise?
Can known operating-state representation transfer to real telemetry without target labels?
Does measured test-bench knowledge transfer to wave/noise-rich ship telemetry?
Can source selection avoid negative transfer while preserving known-class performance?
Do fault signatures learned on superimposed faults match independently observed field fault signatures?

hard_gates: each domain has a separate immutable recording manifest and source digest
all real-vessel recording and voyage identities remain disjoint from fit, calibration and test
zero-shot tracks use no target labels, target feature selection or target threshold tuning
unsupervised adaptation and semi-supervised adaptation are reported as separate tracks with exact target-data access limits
synthetic/virtual-real superimposed fault data are never described as physically observed vessel fault events
real-vessel healthy telemetry is not a substitute for independent field fault labels
all source-domain models and calibrators are frozen before target confirmatory evaluation
report per-fault macro recall, balanced accuracy, event metrics, calibration, false-known and OOD risk-coverage
report the exact independent vessel/engine/voyage count and cluster uncertainty
cross-engine and fleet claims require more than one independent engine identity
published 70.18% zero-shot accuracy is a literature reference, not a benchmark pass or Symtropy result

research_targets_not_achieved.target: Reproduce the paper's 70.18% zero-shot virtual-to-real accuracy under its exact published domain split before comparing new methods.
Exceed the reproduced zero-shot baseline in balanced accuracy and worst-domain macro recall, with independent recording/voyage uncertainty and no target-label access.
Demonstrate source selection does not worsen held-out real-vessel risk versus the best single-source baseline on any preregistered regime.
Make no real-vessel fault-diagnosis claim until independent field fault annotations or permissioned fault-event records exist.

claim_ceiling: Published metadata and reported zero-shot result only. Dataset bytes, license, splits and the reported 70.18% result have not been independently audited or reproduced.
